source_lines_after.80: 1.2 Reversing these reductions also produces the claimed trivial Alexander block. Keep all short vectors first and all long vectors second. A reverse tube addition introduces a new short $x$ with zero column and only the entry 1 in its own long column, and a new long $y$ with zero diagonal. Its couplings to earlier short vectors occupy precisely the new LAST column of $U$, so $U$ stays strictly upper triangular. Its couplings to earlier long vectors give a symmetric new row/column of $W$, with zero new diagonal. Starting from the empty matrix therefore gives $\begin{pmatrix}0&I+U\\U^T&W\end{pmatrix}$ with exactly the advertised conditions. This is an integral symplectic basis of the original lattice; the finite construction below realizes it geometrically rather than assuming that arbitrary integral basis changes are surface homeomorphisms. [F3, F4, algebra]
source_lines_after.82: 1.3 Fix a standard geometric basis $a_i,b_i$ on the actual compact oriented genus-$g$ surface with one boundary circle. Its existence follows by cutting a finite disk-and-handle model of the surface, not from an arbitrary homology basis. Put $\omega(a_i,b_j)=\delta_{ij}$. An annular Dehn twist about an embedded curve $v$ acts by the transvection $T_v(z)=z+\omega(z,v)v$, choosing the twist sign accordingly. This formula is proved by cutting each transverse arc at the annulus: the twisted arc acquires one oriented copy of its core. Curves representing $a_i+a_j$, $b_i+b_j$ and $a_i+b_j$ for $i\ne j$ are embedded band sums on distinct handles. The joining arc lies in the complement of the other standard handles; the band gives the indicated homology class. Thus these transvections and their inverses are actual boundary-fixed surface homeomorphisms (smooth diffeomorphisms in the smooth model). [F5, construct]
source_lines_after.84: 1.4 For orthogonal $u,v$, direct expansion gives $T_{u+v}T_u^{-1}T_v^{-1}(z)=z+\omega(z,u)v+\omega(z,v)u$. [F5, construct]
source_lines_after.86: 1.5 Taking $u=a_i,v=b_j$, $i\ne j$, realizes the elementary block-GL operation $a_j$ to $a_j+a_i$ and $b_i$ to $b_i-b_j$. Its powers realize arbitrary integral elementary additions. Handle permutations and simultaneous sign reversal of $a_i,b_i$ are also realized; the latter is the square of the two-twist rotation on that handle. Euclidean elimination consequently realizes every block action $(x,y)$ to $(A x,A^{-T}y)$ for $A\in\operatorname{GL}_g(\mathbb Z)$. Likewise the $a_i$ and $a_i+a_j$ twists realize every symmetric upper shear, because the diagonal rank-one matrices and the identity $(e_i+e_j)(e_i+e_j)^T-E_{ii}-E_{jj}=E_{ij}+E_{ji}$ generate all symmetric integral matrices; the $b_i$ analogues realize every symmetric lower shear. [F5, construct]
source_lines_after.88: 1.6 Here is a complete generation argument, so this is not an appeal to mapping-class surjectivity. Given a primitive vector $v=(x,y)$, first interchange the $a$ and $b$ directions on a handle if necessary to make $x$ nonzero. A block-GL operation makes $x=(d,0,\ldots,0)$, $d>0$. If some $y_j$ is not divisible by $d$, reduce $d$ strictly: for $j=1$ use the ordinary Euclidean two-twist $\operatorname{SL}_2$ algorithm on $(d,y_1)$; for $j\ne1$ an upper diagonal shear inserts $y_j$ in $x_j$, then block-GL Euclidean reduction replaces $d$ by $\gcd(d,y_j)$. Repeat. The positive integer $d$ decreases until every $y_j$ is divisible by $d$; primitivity then forces $d=1$. A lower symmetric shear with first column $-y$ clears $y$ while keeping $x=e_1$. Thus an actual finite product of the specified twists takes every primitive vector to $a_1$. [F5, construct]
source_lines_after.90: 2.1 Let $A$ be an arbitrary symplectic integral matrix. Apply this procedure to its first column, so the resulting matrix fixes $a_1$. Its image of $b_1$ has the form $b_1+c a_1+z$, with $z$ in the span $W$ of the remaining handles. The displayed orthogonal-transvection combination for $u=a_1$ and each basis vector $v$ of $W$ fixes $a_1$. Its $k$-th power subtracts $k v$ from that image of $b_1$ and only changes its $a_1$ coefficient in addition. Use these powers to clear all coordinates of $z$. Then a power of $T_{a_1}$ clears $c$. The resulting matrix fixes both $a_1,b_1$, and hence restricts symplectically to $W$. Induct on $g$. We have reduced $A$ to the identity by actual twists; reversing the finite list realizes $A$. In particular the symplectic lattice basis from the preceding primitive-vector/tube reduction is represented by an ACTUAL geometric basis, with disjoint short curves, disjoint long curves and exactly one transverse short–long intersection on each matching pair. [F5, construct] ∎
